title: Models of set theory: membership and external viewpoints

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 75–76 (§18, Theorems 18.1–18.3 and set/class relativization conventions); revision 2026-01-31

summary: Interpret membership in a set-sized structure, resolve the countable-model paradox, and separate internal axioms from external well-foundedness and transitivity.
abstract: How can a countable collection of objects form a universe that contains an uncountable set? A model of set theory specifies both its objects and the relation it calls membership; its assertions about sets and functions quantify only over those objects. If ZFC is consistent, completeness supplies a countable model, and compactness also supplies a model with an infinite descending membership chain visible from outside. Such a chain can coexist with the model's Foundation axiom because that axiom tests only collections represented inside the model. With the additional assumption that membership is externally well-founded, the Mostowski collapse instead gives an isomorphic model on a transitive set. Restricting each quantifier to a chosen domain explains satisfaction in actual-membership structures and gives a precise, formula-by-formula meaning to statements about definable proper classes.
